evidence_loop.label: correcting a host claim that was wrong in three plugins
evidence_loop.summary: One measurement invalidated two documented claims, and both turned out to be the same defect: a fact written in several places and updated in some of them. The entry-routing contract blamed the decide-registry resolver being unreachable on Codex on an auto-activated skill mode that does not exist for these skills; the measured cause is that a Codex skill mention has no plugin-root variable in its shell. Separately, three personas claimed Codex could not re-inject a checkpoint, while their own manifests register SessionStart with matcher compact on both hosts — so the claim was wrong in one direction and the reference table it contradicted was overstating in the other. The lasting output is not the prose but the guard: one cross-persona contract test replaces what would have been three copies of the same check.

feature_commits.note: Replaces the resolver-unreachable reason with the measured one and scopes checkpoint re-injection to post-compact. The wording is bound to the skill-mention shell on purpose: hook commands DO receive the substituted plugin-root names, so an unscoped claim would trade one falsehood for another.

Founder carried the same claim at nine sites, not the five files a first scan suggested. Rebase-merged so each package keeps its own changelog entry, which is why the subject carries no PR number and this is attested rather than derived.
Designer carried the identical nine sites, including both fields of the packaged interface metadata that Codex renders to users directly.

hardening_commits.note: Moves the checkpoint guard out of the engineer shape test into one cross-persona contract that iterates the personas. Three copies of a claim guarded by three copies of a check is the same one-of-N defect relocated into the tests.

install_method: Owner-driven host-native update of the three bumped packages on both hosts, verified against the manifest before anything was recorded: engineer 0.21.3, founder 0.4.2, designer 0.3.2 on the Claude cache and codex plugin list alike. The Codex /hooks review was an operator action; twelve [hooks.state] entries across four plugins were observed trusted before the attestation was written.
narrative: The loop began as two documentation defects and ended as one lesson repeated three times. Each correction, once measured, revealed another copy the plan had not counted: the engineer fix shipped with commands/checkpoint.md still holding its own copy of the paragraph the SKILL had just corrected, and the founder/designer pass found nine sites per persona where the plan named five files. A line-based scan found different halves on different passes, because the same sentence wraps at a different word in each file; only whitespace-normalized scanning found all of them. Cross-host review caught two defects in the fix itself, both of the class being fixed: the missed command-file copy, and a global negative about Codex substitution that had never been measured and was narrowed to the observation actually taken. Mutation verification earned its place three separate times rather than confirming a foregone conclusion. It found a positive assertion scoped per file where the packaged metadata carries the claim in two fields, the same gap again at row level where a frontmatter line satisfied a file-level check, and literal backslashes this change had introduced into four markdown files, which surfaced only because a mutation that should have failed did not. The release itself corrected an expectation carried into this session: post-release doc-freshness recovery is coupled to the runtime version, so a release that bumps only personas needs the catalog sync and nothing more. That was measured, not assumed, after the earlier release in the same session had needed the full recovery.
